project.name: OurDiary
project.goal: Build a production-ready, private, playful and colorful relationship web app for exactly two partners, with an animated toy train journey, memories, notes, calendar, gallery, letters, bucket list and statistics.
project.design: Modern polished app, rounded cards, cheerful pink, lavender, coral, mint, yellow and sky-blue accents; not a paper or vintage diary.
project.budget: Prefer free tiers and avoid paid dependencies unless approved.

agent_command: Implement the complete OurDiary application in the repository, not just a plan. Inspect existing files first, work incrementally, and validate each phase. Do not create third-party accounts or invent credentials. Build integration code with environment placeholders and provide precise manual setup steps for the owner.

stack.frontend: Next.js App Router, React, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS, shadcn/ui, Lucide React, Motion for React
stack.authorization: Supabase Row Level Security and verified server-side checks
stack.media_storage: Cloudinary for all images and videos

owner_must_create: A Cloudinary account and cloud environment
A Vercel account only when deployment is desired
agent_must_do: Create .env.example containing only placeholder names and descriptions
Document where to find each configuration value in the providers' dashboards
Create .env.local from placeholders only if necessary, ensure it is gitignored, and never commit it
Never ask the owner to paste secrets into the master JSON, chat, source files, or Git repository
Generate SQL migration files and setup instructions; never pretend remote migrations or dashboard settings were applied
If credentials are unavailable, implement the integrations and a clearly marked local demo mode with mock data, without claiming live authentication, storage or synchronization works
security_notes: The Supabase URL and publishable key may be exposed to the browser; RLS is still mandatory
Never expose the Supabase service-role/secret key or Cloudinary API secret to client-side code
Cloudinary API key and secret must be server-only; never prefix them with NEXT_PUBLIC_
Do not use unsigned uploads for real personal media
Use separate development and production environment variables when possible

access_model.signup: Invite-only onboarding; disable open public signup after the two approved accounts are established, where supported by provider settings
access_model.couple: One couple with exactly two approved member user IDs; enforce membership in database and server authorization, not just UI
access_model.profiles: Each partner has a profile, name, avatar and session
access_model.shared_content: Only the two couple members may read or modify authorized shared content
access_model.private_notes: Only the note author may read, list, edit or delete their private notes; do not leak note content or metadata via APIs, counts, joins or Realtime
access_model.writes: Validate user identity, couple membership, resource ownership and input on every mutation
access_model.login: Use Supabase Auth with email/password or magic link; implement proper session handling and protected routes

requirements: Create versioned SQL migrations, foreign keys, indexes and timestamps
Enable and test RLS on every user-content table
Use couple-membership checks in RLS for shared resources
Use author-only RLS for private notes; avoid policies that expose them through shared-memory access
Use secure SQL functions or backend authorization for operations requiring elevated privileges
Use Supabase client/server helpers appropriate for current Next.js and Supabase packages
Store Cloudinary identifiers and metadata in PostgreSQL, not image binaries
Never store passwords in custom tables

cloudinary.purpose: Store and optimize photos and videos uploaded to OurDiary
upload_flow: Authenticated browser requests upload authorization from a Next.js Route Handler
Server validates the Supabase session, couple membership, media type and size
Server issues a short-lived Cloudinary signed upload authorization with controlled folder and parameters
Server verifies and records the uploaded asset metadata in Supabase, linked to an authorized memory
Use server-authorized deletion of assets and associated database records
privacy: Relationship media is sensitive: do not assume Cloudinary's default public delivery URLs are private
Configure an appropriate restricted delivery mode and server-authorized access/signatures; verify provider plan and feature support before promising private delivery
Never persist or return unrestricted public media URLs for private assets
Validate access to a memory before issuing a media URL
Keep secrets server-side and rate-limit upload-signing endpoints
Do not rely on Cloudinary folders as an access-control boundary
optimization: Use consistent thumbnail, card and detail sizes
Use automatic format and quality where compatible with the chosen secure delivery setup
Limit video file sizes and duration to control free-tier usage
Track storage, bandwidth and transformation credits; keep original backups elsewhere

journey: Animated toy train that follows path direction
memories: Create, edit, delete and search memories
Date, story, mood, category, location and tags
notes: Shared notes visible to both partners
Private notes visible only to their author
Enforce visibility using RLS, not frontend filtering alone
letters: Future unlock dates enforced server-side, not just hidden in UI

requirements: Refresh authorized shared memories, events and notes across both logged-in devices
Configure Realtime publications and policies correctly
Do not broadcast private-note content to the other partner
Handle reconnects and concurrent edits gracefully

phases: 1. Inspect repository, scaffold Next.js, create design system and responsive layout
2. Implement realistic local demo data and fully interactive dashboard, memories, notes and navigation
3. Build animated SVG train journey and station interactions
4. Build calendar, gallery, letters, bucket list, statistics and settings
5. Add Supabase Auth, onboarding and protected routes using placeholders
6. Write Supabase SQL migrations, RLS policies and database integration
7. Add secure Cloudinary signed upload, restricted delivery and deletion integration
8. Add Supabase Realtime and two-device updates
9. Test security, accessibility, responsive behavior and production build; document deployment
checks: E2E tests for memory CRUD and profile access
Test private notes cannot be fetched by the other user
Test unauthorized upload-signature requests are rejected
output_expectations: Create working project files and reusable components
Provide README with exact Supabase and Cloudinary dashboard setup instructions
Explain how the owner applies SQL migrations and configures auth redirects
Clearly distinguish mock mode from fully connected mode
Report what was actually tested and what still requires real credentials

definition_of_done: Both authorized partners can log in separately
Only approved couple members can access relationship data
Shared memories and notes synchronize across devices
Private notes cannot be read by the other partner, including via direct API requests
Photos/videos are uploaded to Cloudinary with authorized signed uploads and appropriately restricted delivery
Cloudinary asset IDs and memory metadata are stored in Supabase
Train journey, calendar and gallery update when memories change
All advertised controls work on desktop and mobile
No credentials are embedded in code, JSON or Git history
Project builds successfully and includes reproducible setup instructions
